subject: KV warm-up / microburst crediting — concrete examples requested
messages:
From: Tom Liu <tom@heliumcloud.io>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: billing@heliumcloud.io
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected charges from microbursts and KV cold starts

Sergio,

We ran into a billing surprise on this month's invoice — a large portion of the overage looks like it came from a flurry of short requests (microbursts) during a deploy and a subsequent set of cold-started KV-cache misses. The attached CSV has the sample spike (120 calls over 6 minutes, median request 420 tokens, many with ~0 prefix tokens).

Two specific asks:
- Can you confirm how microbursts are billed today (per-request vs rolling window)?
- Do we get any implicit credit for KV cache warmups (first N requests counted differently)? If not, can you provide an example calculation of how we'd be billed for the attached spike?

We'd like concrete numbers to show our finance team so we can decide whether to request a contract amendment or a transient credit.

Appreciate the help — Tom

--
Tom Liu
Head of Platform
HeliumCloud
From: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Tom Liu <tom@heliumcloud.io>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, billing@heliumcloud.io
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges from microbursts and KV cold starts

Tom — thanks for the sample and for flagging this. I pulled the attach and ran an initial pass. I want to align on a clear set of examples so your finance team can understand the delta and we can propose a remediation if needed. Looping in Grace and Ben to confirm the math and policy options.

High-level notes (first pass):
- Microburst billing: default is per-token per-request (no smoothing). That means 120 requests * 420 tokens = 50,400 token-charge for that window (before any aggregation rules).
- KV warmup behavior: we currently do not have an explicit "warmup credit" built-in; first requests that populate KV state are charged normally. However we have two possible mitigations:
  1) One-off credit: grant a manual credit (example below).
  2) Policy change: a short-term tolerance window where we bill against a 60s rolling median for accounts flagged as "deploy spikes".

Concrete examples I propose we provide HeliumCloud so they can see the impact:
Example A (today): 120 calls * 420 tokens = 50,400 tokens billed. If rounding/minimums apply at 10-token quantum, that's effectively unchanged (rounded up to nearest 10).
Example B (warmup-credit path): define warmup N=30 requests per model-instance; mark first 30 requests as 100% credit. Billing: (120 - 30) * 420 = 37,800 tokens billed — a 25% reduction.
Example C (rolling-window smoothing): compute per-minute median token usage across the 6-minute window and bill 95th percentile minute instead of raw sum; for your sample that results in ~28,000 tokens billed (approx).

Grace / Ben — can you confirm the rounding behavior per-token quantum (we have sometimes used a 10-token floor vs 1-token precise metering for streaming calls) and whether we can quickly produce both CSV and invoice delta for Tom's sample?

Next steps: I'll prepare the three example invoices (A/B/C) and a short note on policy implications. If HeliumCloud prefers, we can propose a transient credit while they instrument warm caches or we can offer an account-level warmup flag for dedicated fleets.

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, Tom Liu <tom@heliumcloud.io>, billing@heliumcloud.io
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges from microbursts and KV cold starts

Sergio / Tom — ran the numbers off Tom's CSV and attached a short table (kv-warmup-proposal.pdf) with precise math. Summary here:

1) Rounding quantum: for hosted API streaming we bill at 1-token precision. For batched non-streamed generation we apply a 10-token quantum for invoice line reduction. HeliumCloud's spike is from streamed-like short calls, so 1-token precision applies (no extra rounding benefit).

2) CSV sample math (verbatim):
- Total requests: 120
- Median tokens/request: 420
- Raw token sum: 50,400 tokens
- With current per-token billing (no warmup): 50,400 tokens => at agreed rate $0.0006/token => $30.24 charge for that window.

3) Warmup-credit proposal (concrete):
- Policy: first 25 requests per model-instance within a rolling 5-minute window flagged as "warmup" and credited 100%
- Effect on sample: billable tokens = (120 - 25) * 420 = 40,500 tokens => $24.30 (20% drop).

4) Microburst smoothing (example formula):
- Compute per-60s buckets, take the 75th percentile bucket during the incident and multiply by #buckets where requests occurred. For this sample that approach yields ~32,400 tokens => $19.44. This is intentionally conservative compared to 95th percentile to limit holiday claims.

5) Operational notes:
- Warmup credits are straightforward to grant retroactively for an account, or we can enable an automatic warmup flag for your Dedicated fleets (needs SRE).
- Smoothing requires a small billing-engine change but is implementable as an account-level setting; estimated 2-week engineering turnaround for a clean rollout.

Tom — if you want a one-off goodwill credit I can prepare the amount now. Otherwise, pick which policy you prefer and we'll send a formal proposal and an updated invoice example.

—Grace
Senior Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Tom Liu <tom@heliumcloud.io>, billing@heliumcloud.io
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges from microbursts and KV cold starts

Quick note — I reviewed Grace's numbers and they look good. Recommend we:
1) Offer a one-time credit equal to the delta between example A and example B ($30.24 - $24.30 = $5.94) to resolve this quickly;
2) Offer HeliumCloud the warmup-flag on their next Dedicated rollout as a longer-term mitigation;
3) Draft a KB article showing the math and when to expect warmup credits.

Happy to approve the credit; Sergio, go ahead and apply and I'll track internally.

—Ben
Revenue Lead, Americas
Redwood Inference
